t: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the Federal building and United States courthouse referred to in section 1 shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Tom Stagg United States Court House”.

fable.w: This is a boilerplate references clause that deems existing mentions of a federal building to refer to its new name, the Tom Stagg United States Court House. The tempting reading is that the word "regulation" signals rulemaking, but it only lists a type of record in which the building's name may appear; it does not authorize or require any regulation. No party outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue over any federal decision.
fable.s: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States

opus.w: The section only says that references in federal records to a courthouse will now be read as references to the "Tom Stagg United States Court House." The word "regulation" is part of a list of record types. It does not give an agency power to make rules, so it is not a rulemaking provision. No outside party takes part in any federal decision.
opus.b: This section just renames a building. The only word that might look relevant is "regulation," but here it appears in a list of records that will now refer to the new name. Nothing in the section gives an agency power to make rules, and no outside party is consulted, given a hearing, or allowed to comment.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a purely administrative directive regarding the naming convention for a federal building. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public comment periods, or requirements to consult with states, tribes, or the public.
qwen_chat.s: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the Federal building and United States courthouse referred to in section 1 shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Tom Stagg United States Court House”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that renaming a building involves public input or consultation, but the text itself contains no such requirement. It is purely a directive on how to refer to a specific building in official records.
